text: The fourteen legacy acceptance criteria AC1 to AC14 of RWB-E2-026 are owned by RWB-P5-E2026-APP; this story is a secondary slice of the same legacy key and carries eight new criteria that test only the treatment-side request and use.
why: One legacy capability cannot have two owners of the same criteria, and the Work Package splits this key across P5, P6, S2 and the integration harness.
read: Work Package B-S2-06; RWB-E2-026 section 7; RWB-P5-E2026-APP section 7
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-document and the solution architect
impact: No legacy criterion is restated or lost, and the engine's behaviour is proved in P5.

text: The generation is consumed as the published REST contract with a mock: one hop, a 2 s timeout, a breaker and no call chain; the operation identifier, the activity name and the shape of the S2 value set on the wire are taken from RWB-P5-E2026-CON and from this story's design over the treatment row.
why: The legacy call was in process and no source names the REST operation identifier, the activity name or the wire shape of the values rwb-treatment supplies.
read: DP-11 and ADR-020; RWB-P5-E2026-CON sections 12.1, 12.2 and 12.5; TSD S2 T3.1
impact: S2 builds on Day 1 against the contract and its fake, and a renamed field or a different timeout fails the contract test rather than a customer document.

text: Only identifiers, codes, amounts, dates and versions travel on the request this service supplies, on the event it writes and in its logs; a name, a national ID number and a title-doc number are never supplied, stored, logged or published by rwb-treatment.
why: The merge values of a template include personal values, and the target reads personal data only through its owner and never copies it.
read: CTL-11 and DL26; Architecture v5 slide 11; RWB-E2-026 BR11 and section 17
impact: The personal values stay in rwb-source-data and rwb-case and reach the engine from their owners; no personal value exists in rwb_treatment, on the topic or in a log.

text: The workflow kit, the guard, the inbox, the outbox and decision-record client libraries, the embedded Drools runtime and the parameters and reference-data clients are service-template capabilities with no build row of their own; the template catalogue and the merge fields are read only through the owners' answers of P6 rwb-comms and P5 rwb-document and never as tables.
why: The service template supplies these capabilities once and the Ownership Map, not the legacy module layout, decides who owns the catalogue.
read: Architecture v5 slides 20 and 41; Ownership Map v1; DP-01; Template and Rules §R5.5
confirm: Platform library owner and the solution architect
impact: The story adds no H row for a template capability and reads no rwb_comms or rwb_document table.

text: SCR-14 Treatment record and SCR-15 Settlement offer are served by the gateway-bff composite route, which merges this service's treatment read with the document read of rwb-document, one hop each and read only; this story serves no screen field list and no layout.
why: No screen reads one database in the target, and the route specification belongs to the edge contract.
read: DP-19; RWB-PLT-N001-CON; FSD S2 screens SCR-14 and SCR-15
confirm: Edge story owner and the screen owners
impact: The reference and the pinned version reach the screens through the route; the browser calls no owner service directly.

text: The local decision-record library dependency that DP-03 adds is supplied by the platform contract RWB-PLT-E1027-CON on Day 1, so the story keeps Depends on (build) None and builds against its fake; the other H rows the pattern table adds are faked the same way until their platform stories publish.
why: The plan's build list for this story is None while DP-03, DP-06, DP-07, DP-09, DP-15 and DP-19 each add a platform contract.
read: Template and Rules §R5.5 and §R5.7; plan slice RWB-S2-E2026-APP; RWB-PLT-E1027-CON
impact: Day-1 build is possible with the fakes, and the plan's build list needs a later correction on the dependency map.

text: The treatment row carries the contract-document reference and the pinned template version in two nullable columns added by this story's Flyway version, with the index ix_treatment_contract_document, because TSD S2 T3.1 gives neither column and no source names them.
why: The reference and the version have to live on the record of the treatment, and no field of the treatment table carries them.
read: TSD S2 T3.1; DP-15; RWB-E2-026 section 13
confirm: Solution architect and the S2 data owner
impact: No sibling story narrows the two columns; a later field-list version replaces the design names, and the migration is additive with no backfill.

text: The name and payload of the generation event and the decision code it carries, and the operation names of the parameters and reference-data reads, are stated by no source; this story names the event rwb.treatment.ContractDocumentGenerated.v1 with the payload of 12.3, carries decision code D6.4, and takes the two read operations from their contracts.
why: The event catalogue gives rwb-treatment two events only and the parameters and reference-data operations are unnamed in the sources.
read: Architecture v5 slides 18, 42 and 43; DP-06, DP-07 and DP-09; RWB-P5-E2026-CON
confirm: Event catalogue owner and the P3 contract owner
impact: The event name is provisional until the catalogue is published; no consumer is registered in wave 2, so a later rename costs no migration.
